# Q3 — D8's floor check on the merged pool's reachability failures

Source: `falsifier/out/tos-merged-report.json` (merged dump, 1,397 slots, 1,284 reachable). The 113
slots with `node.within == false`: 24 falsifier (control-reachable) + 89 unreachable-from-both, over 61
artworks. Measured at git 16e84b75 via `tos/identity/pin.sh`. Rates through `src/stats` (Wilson).

Every one of the 113 endorsed colours IS an exact triple of its artwork (0 slots with zero exact
pixels), median exact share 1.46e-5, median bar-neighbourhood share 2.08e-3.

## Classification (MECE, tested in this order)

| class | all 113 | falsifier 24 | both 89 | floor change recovers? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| absent-from-image (bar mass 0) | 0 | 0 | 0 | no |
| above-floor-region (largest bar-coherent region >= 5e-4) | 42 | 18 | 24 | NO |
| dispersed-no-region (largest region < 8 px) | 15 | 0 | 15 | no |
| antialias-only (region >= 8 px, max inradius < 2 px) | 30 | 2 | 28 | no |
| below-floor-concentrated-mark | 26 | 4 | 22 | YES |

Class medians (bar share / largest-region area fraction / max inradius px):
above-floor 1.32e-2 / 7.77e-3 / 6.4; antialias-only 1.01e-3 / 5.37e-5 / 1.4; dispersed 2.11e-4 /
1.71e-5 / 1.0; below-floor-concentrated 2.24e-3 / 2.75e-4 / 2.2.
The filament test reads the maximum inradius over the colour's regions (top 128 by area), i.e. "does a
compact region of this colour exist anywhere", which is the question a floor change turns on.

## Recoverable share

- all failing slots: 26/113 = 23.0% (95% CI 16.2%-31.6%) | n=113 | Wilson score interval at 95%
- falsifier slots only: 4/24 = 16.7% (95% CI 6.7%-35.9%) | n=24
- unreachable from both: 22/89 = 24.7% (95% CI 16.9%-34.6%) | n=89
- CAVEAT: the 113 slots are clustered inside 61 artworks; the Wilson interval treats them as
  independent and is therefore optimistic.

Where the floor would have to sit. The 26 recoverable slots' largest-region area fractions: min
3.91e-5, p25 1.31e-4, median 2.75e-4, p75 3.13e-4, max 3.66e-4 — all below `MIN_NODE_AREA_FRACTION`
5e-4. Sweep: a floor at 3e-4 recovers 9 of 26 (0 of the 4 falsifier slots), 2e-4 recovers 16 (2), 1e-4
recovers 22 (2), 5e-5 recovers 24 (2), 3.9e-5 recovers all 26 (4). Recovering the falsifier's own four
needs a floor ~12.8x lower than today's.

## What the largest class actually is (second pass, `above-floor.json`)

42/113 slots — and 18 of the 24 falsifier slots, i.e. 75% of the pre-registered numerator — have a
bar-coherent region at or above the floor already. The floor never removed them. Walking each region's
pixels up every lane's tree to the nearest RETAINED node (cut: retained area > 4x region area means the
region's own scale was not retained; median observed ratio 6.4):

| mechanism | of 42 | of the 18 falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| retention-lost-the-scale (`selectStableNodes` kept no node at the region's scale) | 24 | 7 |
| representative-rule-lost-the-colour (a node IS at the region's scale; `representativeColor`'s bar-density mode elected a different triple — median bar ratio 1.44) | 18 | 11 |

## Verdict on D8

D8's floor hypothesis explains at most 4 of 24 falsifier slots (16.7%) and 26 of 113 failures (23.0%).
It is real but small. 75% of the falsifier's numerator is ALREADY above the area floor, and inside that
the majority mechanism is the REPRESENTATIVE-COLOUR RULE (11 of 18), not stability retention (7 of 18).
A further 45 of 113 (39.8%) have no retainable region at all — the endorsed colour exists only as a
blend or as scattered pixels, and neither a smaller floor nor a stability-based criterion reaches them.
Moving `MIN_NODE_AREA_FRACTION` toward a stability-based retention is therefore a defensible but
minority repair; the larger return is in how a retained node's representative is chosen.
